entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and  learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with G.R. Case No.1038 of 2025 pending in the Court of learned SDJM, Rourkela, arising out of Jharipani P.S. Case No. 90 of 2025 for commission of offences punishable under Sections 419/420 of IPC.

3. It is submitted by the learned counsel that an essentially commercial transaction inter se between the parties has been given the colour of criminality, and as such, the FIR ought not to be instituted in the first place.
4.
Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for pre-arrest bail.
5. Learned counsel for the informant on the other hand also opposes the prayer for pre-arrest bail and submits that from the very inception, the Petitioner had mens rea to commit the offence.

Hence,
no leniency ought to be shown.
6. Admittedly, the occurrence relates to the year 2015 to 2024 as borne out from the FIR.

7. It is submitted by the learned counsel on instruction that the Petitioner does not have any criminal proclivity of similar nature, though he is stated to be involved in Kamakhya Nagar P.S. Case Pranab Chakraborty vs State Of Odisha And .... Opposite ... on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18306757/
1 No.41 of 2012 under Sections 297, 37 and 38 of IPC.
8.

entities.text: Kamakhya Nagar P.S. Case Pranab Chakraborty vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the informant that though the matter was referred to mediation, the Petitioner could not cooperate, for which the mediation became unsuccessful.

9. Per contra it is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the same ought not to weigh with this Court in considering the prayer of the Petitioner for pre-arrest bail in the light of the allegations.

10. Considering the rival submissions, this Court directs that on surrendering within three weeks hence and moving for bail, the Petitioner shall be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as deemed just and proper subject to verification of criminal antecedent of similar nature.
11. If it comes to the fore that the Petitioner has any such criminal antecedent, this order shall not be given effect to.
12. It is needless to state that the Petitioner shall cooperate with the ongoing investigation.
13. Accordingly, the ABLAPL stands disposed of.
